subject: vintage

bbr.name: Berry Bros. & Rudd, Barolo 2018 vintage report

wineindep.name: The Wine Independent, Barolo and Barbaresco 2017, 2018 and 2019

claims.claim: Winter was damp and snowy after the dry 2017. A sharp cold snap in late February left 60 to 70 cm of snow.
claims.note: Two sources agree. The snow figure is from Chiarlo.

claims.claim: Spring was extremely wet. May brought 21 to 25 rainy days. Growing-season rain was about 923 mm, roughly 35% above average. Wet soil kept tractors out, and downy and powdery mildew needed quick treatment.
claims.quote: one of the wettest springs ever recorded
claims.note: Quote is from Berry Bros. Four sources agree on the wet spring. The 923 mm figure is from Vinous.

claims.claim: Flowering was uneven, with many aborted flowers, after the May rain.
claims.note: One source read in full. A search summary of another report says rain at flowering hurt fruit set.

claims.claim: No notable frost. Hail in August hit some vineyards badly, but it was very local and neighbouring plots were untouched.
claims.note: Vinous says no frost or hail of note. Berry Bros. mentions local August hail.

claims.claim: From mid-June summer was warm and mostly dry, with highs near 35 C in early August. Cool nights from late August helped aromas. Soil water reserves carried the vines.
claims.note: Three sources agree. A different producer source says September was very warm with small day-night swings, so nights varied.

claims.claim: Harvest was regular to slightly late. Rain in September led some growers to pick earlier than planned. Others waited into October for phenolic ripeness.
claims.note: No exact dates found. Chiarlo calls it regular timing, slightly early. Vinous and Berry Bros. lean later.

claims.claim: Yields were generally decent to high, helped by the vine releasing energy stored after 2017. Not every source agrees.
claims.note: Vinous says high. Chiarlo says normal Nebbiolo clusters. A search summary says the Consorzio reported limited Nebbiolo yields. No official figure found.

claims.claim: Nebbiolo is perfumed and lighter than 2015 to 2017, with silky tannins. Many wines are bright and juicy with fresh acidity. Some are light or fleeting, a few dilute or green.
claims.note: Quote is from Berry Bros. Critics split on quality. Vinous calls it uneven.

claims.claim: Quality varies by producer and site. La Morra, Verduno, Brunate and Cerequio are named for standout wines. Some producers declassified crus or skipped them.
claims.note: Declassification examples include Massolino, Gaja and Produttori del Barbaresco.

claims.claim: Many wines are ready to drink now. The best could last 15 to 20 years.
claims.note: Merchant and critic view, not a formal window.

conflicts: Quality: Berry Bros. praises finesse and charm. Vinous calls the vintage uneven, and a Flatiron summary says mixed. Treat it as producer dependent.
Yields: Vinous says high. A search summary says the Consorzio reported limited Nebbiolo yields. Chiarlo says normal Nebbiolo bunches.
September: Chiarlo and Berry Bros. describe cool nights, while another critic says September was very warm with little night cooling.
gaps: No Consorzio di Tutela report read, so no official harvest dates or volumes.
Vietti and Jancis Robinson reports not read. No exact harvest dates found.

sheet.vintage: 2018 followed a very wet spring, then a warm, dry summer. The Nebbiolo is perfumed and silky, lighter than the years around it, and quality depends on the producer.
